A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CSPCL research. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable and can be matched across revisions. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains Appendices A–D and a conference checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments on PIXray and OPIXray, hyperparameter and component ablations, and feature and detection visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds PIDray and CLCXray results, plus a briefly reported COCO result in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The classifier-weight prototypes, query grouping, ITA and IAR losses, and decoder training algorithm remain unchanged. C-AO-DETR names the existing AO-DETR plus CSPCL combination. Correcting Algorithm 1's title from MMCL to CSPCL does not change its procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond retained PIXray and OPIXray evaluations, v2 adds PIDray, including easy, hard and hidden scenarios, and CLCXray's fine-grained cutter and liquid-container detection task. Appendix D also reports limited evaluation on natural-image COCO, expanding coverage beyond X-ray imagery.

E2.justification: New Tables 3 and 5 substantially expand reported comparators, including Faster and Mask R-CNN, FCOS, ATSS, DN-DETR, SDANet, ForkNet, Cascade and Dynamic R-CNN, DOAM, LAreg, LAcls and PIXDet. The original detector and N-pair/InfoNCE comparisons remain. IIC and ICE receive discussion, not empirical comparison.

E3.justification: The original ResNet-50, 320×320, 12-epoch configuration remains. The new PIDray comparison introduces Swin-L, 512×512 inputs, 14 epochs and 240 queries, with difficulty-specific AP reporting. Appendix A also evaluates C-AO-DETR with Swin-L and 512×512 inputs. These are additional experimental configurations, not revisions establishing improved performance under the original settings.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a brief applicability check asking whether CSPCL also benefits natural-image detection, reporting only about 0.1% AP improvement on COCO without detailed settings. Existing component, hyperparameter and decoder-layer ablations, t-SNE analyses, confidence/IoU plots and attention case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its results. v2's checklist explicitly acknowledges absent statistical-significance reporting but introduces no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds PIDray results, including 70.8 overall AP for C-AO-DETR, CLCXray results including 63.1 AP, and the brief COCO finding. Retained benchmark scores otherwise remain stable, with two corrections: N-pair small-object AP changes from 237 to 23.7, and the layer-5 ablation's reported difference changes from +2.3 to -3.7 while its 60.6 AP remains unchanged.

T1.justification: The CSPCL mathematics is unchanged apart from equation grouping and numbering. Appendix B reproduces published IIC and ICE loss formulas for qualitative comparison; it adds no substantive derivation, formal assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central prototype-alignment and CSP-loss contributions remain. The abstract and contribution list extend validation claims from two to four X-ray datasets and add a claim of advancing state-of-the-art performance. They also qualify the efficiency claim specifically as unchanged inference complexity.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly identifies limited applicability to natural-image detection through the small COCO benefit. Appendix A discusses the tradeoff between Swin-L's parameter count and computation reduced by smaller inputs. Appendix C elaborates the existing alignment explanation without replacing it.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the abstract's future code-release promise with a public repository link, although its checklist still says release is pending. It documents backbone, input size, epoch and query settings for the added PIDray experiment. Existing hardware, software and optimizer disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B substantially extends comparative positioning through explicit critiques of IIC and ICE regarding intra-class diversity and inter-class repulsion. Added detector comparisons and citations to dual-view, few-shot and cross-domain X-ray research broaden the research context. The original positioning relative to MMCL remains.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the overall narrative remain intact. Local revisions clarify loss descriptions, correct Algorithm 1's name, update author information, and place Generalization before Ablation Experiments. Appendices and a checklist are added without extensive rewriting of the retained exposition.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a single-column conference format. Separate loss figures are merged, t-SNE panels are rearranged with a simplified legend, and detection visualizations are combined. The PIXray and OPIXray tables become one table, and new PIDray and CLCXray tables are added.

improvement.justification: The added benchmark comparisons, explicit COCO limitation and numerical corrections improve evidential breadth and accuracy. Their benefit is limited by heterogeneous comparison settings, no matched AO-DETR control on CLCXray, and unchanged uncertainty reporting. A new claim also overstates PIDray hidden-subset performance: Table 3 reports ForkNet at 58.6 AP versus C-AO-DETR at 56.9. Together with conflicting code-release statements, these weaknesses constrain the otherwise useful improvement.
